Open Start and type your company name and your own numbers in the yellow cells: weight tolerance, yield target, most hours for one maker in a day, service warning days and the share of a batch you test.

Record every batch on Batches (a batch is one production run with its own batch number): the units made, the issue, the quality result, the cure days and the lots. Yield, days to ready and waste cost fill in.
Yield means good units as a share of planned units. Yield by product shows it for the last 90 days against the target of each product.
Use Production plan before every week: it adds the hours of each maker for each day and flags a day that is over your limit. Maker workload shows the same by week.

Cure shelf lists the batches that rest before they are ready (the cure). Enter the start date and the cure days; the ready date and the days left fill in. Fill Released on when the batch leaves the shelf.
Log every check on Quality checks. For a weight check type the measured grams; the gap against the target and your tolerance fills in. Failed batches holds each batch that failed or needs a recheck.
Label checks only record what is printed. Check your own local rules for what a label must show. Retained samples keeps a unit of each batch and tells you when a check is due.
Keep Equipment, Equipment downtime and the Cleaning log up to date. The service status and the missed tasks show on the dashboard.
Lot use records which lot of wax, oil or fragrance went into which batch. A lot is one delivery of a material with its own lot number.
Rework and seconds records the units remade, relabelled or sold as seconds. Production demand turns the forecast into the batches to start.

Use the 14 calculators before you plan: scaling a formula, yield and waste, cure dates, hours, day load, batches from demand, wax, soap moulds, cooling, rework, batch numbers, sample size and weight tolerance.
Read the Production Dashboard and the Charts every week: yield, waste, quality results, planned hours, equipment and cleaning.
Reorder points, lots, supplier orders and stock counts in one workbook
Reorder points, lots, supplier orders and counts for candle and soap makers
Reorder point from use and lead days
the stock level at which you order again, from the average use a day, the lead days and your safety days, so orders go out before the shelf is empty
Days of cover for every material
34 materials with the stock on hand, the days it lasts, the date it runs out and a suggested order rounded to the pack size
Lot register with first in first out
each delivery has its lot number, use-by date and value left, and the oldest lot is ranked first so it is opened first and a lot used out of order shows in red
Supplier order tracker with late flags
every order shows the expected date, the days late of an open order, the lead time and the date to pay, so a late order is chased the same day
orders, share on time, issues and days to arrive of each supplier become one score from 0 to 100 against your target for the quarterly review
the system quantity against the quantity counted, the gap in money and a tolerance check, so a gap is a number and not a feeling
every spill, expired lot and failed batch with its reason and value, so you see what waste costs by month and by reason
the pack price plus delivery divided by the kilograms of two suppliers, with the yearly difference at your use
24 products with units on hand, curing and reserved, the days of cover and a flag, so the shop hides what runs out and a batch is planned in time
jars, tins, boxes, labels and tape with days of cover and the next delivery date, so the packer is never stopped by a missing box
each change in what a supplier charges with the percent, the direction and the month, so a rising cost reaches your prices early
each delivery checked at the door with the quantity ordered and received and its condition, so a short or damaged delivery is reported the same day

Materials with cost, unit, supplier and lead time
The 34 materials with category, unit, cost per kilogram or piece, supplier, lead days and pack size; the cost per 100 grams, the stock on hand and the open orders fill in.
Material stock with days of cover and the reorder point
One row for each material with the stock on hand, the reorder point (the stock level at which you order again) and the average use a day; days of cover, value and a suggested order fill in.
Lots with use-by dates and first in first out order
One row for each delivery of a material with its own lot number (a lot); the value left, the days to the use-by date and the first in first out rank fill in, so the oldest lot is opened first.
Purchase orders to suppliers with late flags
One row for each order to a supplier with the quantity, the cost and the expected date; the line value, the days late, the state, the lead time and the payment date fill in.
Suppliers with contact, lead days and terms
The 12 suppliers with the contact, phone, lead days and payment terms; the open orders, their value and the spend of the last 12 months fill in.
One row for each change in what a supplier charges for a material, with the old and the new cost; the change in percent and the direction fill in.
Receiving log with shortfalls and condition
One row for each delivery checked at the door, with the quantity ordered and received and its condition; the shortfall, the supplier and the check fill in.
Stock counts with variance and its value
One row for each count of a material on the shelf, with the quantity in the system and the quantity counted; the variance, its value and the tolerance check fill in.
Stock adjustments with the reason and the value
One row for each change made to the stock numbers outside a delivery or a batch, with the reason and who approved it; the cost for each unit and the value fill in.
Finished goods stock with days of cover
The 24 products with units on hand, curing, reserved and the reorder point; the days of cover, the value and the reorder flag fill in.
Packaging stock with days of cover
The jars, tins, boxes, labels and tape on the shelf with the reorder point and the average use a day; the days of cover, the value and the reorder flag fill in.
Weekly reorder list with the order value
One row for each material to order in a week, with the stock, the reorder point, the quantity and the supplier; the order value fills in, so Monday ends with the orders placed.
Material usage by month with cost per batch
One row for each main material and month, with the quantity and value used, the batches it went into and the stock value held at month end; the cost for each batch fills in.
Waste and write-offs with reason and value
One row for each material thrown away, spilled or written off, with the quantity, the reason and the value; the unit fills in.
Supplier issues with the days open
One row for each late, short, damaged or wrong delivery or invoice problem, with the units affected and when it was resolved; the days open fill in.
One row for each supplier; the orders of the last 12 months, the share on time, the issues, the average days to arrive and a score from 0 to 100 fill in from the orders and the issues.
One row for each material or component in a batch of a product, with the quantity and the cost of a unit of it; the cost of the line and the cost for each finished unit fill in.
Lead times promised and actual by supplier
One row for each recent delivery with the days the supplier promised and the days it took; the days late and an on-time check fill in.
Storage locations with the last check
The shelves, cabinets, rooms and bins where materials live with the number of items and the date of the last check; the days since the check and a due flag fill in.
